sections.label: Corporate Income Tax Rebate and Carry-Back
sections.summary: A 25% Corporate Income Tax Rebate capped at $15,000 per company is granted for YA 2020, and qualifying deductions may be carried back up to three preceding YAs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, to help companies with cash flow, a Corporate Income Tax Rebate of 25% of tax payable, capped at $15,000 per company, is granted for Year of Assessment or YA 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, also to help businesses with cash flow, qualifying deductions for YA2020 may be carried back up to three immediate preceding YAs, instead of one immediate preceding YA.

sections.label: Double Tax Deduction Internationalisation Extension
sections.summary: The Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation scheme is extended until 31 December 2025 to encourage firms to internationalise.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Third, to continue encouraging our firms to internationalise, the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation scheme has been extended until 31 December 2025.

sections.label: Surcharge on Tax Avoidance Adjustments
sections.summary: A surcharge equal to 50% of additional income tax payable from Comptroller adjustments counteracting tax avoidance arrangements will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, to further deter tax avoidance arrangements, we will introduce a surcharge equal to 50% of the amount of additional income tax payable as a result of the adjustments by the Comptroller of Income Tax to counteract tax avoidance arrangements.

sections.label: Income Tax Amendment Bill 2020
sections.summary: The Income Tax (Amendment) Bill of 2020 implements tax changes previously discussed at the Budget Statement and supplementary Budgets.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Income Tax (Amendment) Bill of 2020 implements the tax changes that were previously discussed and debated at this Government's Budget Statement together with a host of supplementary Budgets.

sections.label: Clauses 30 and 63 Avoidance Issues
sections.summary: Clauses 30 and 63 explicitly take on avoidance issues.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A number of amendments, in particular, the two clauses, clauses 30 and 63 explicitly take on avoidance issues.

sections.label: Clause 15 Exemptions and GST Timing
sections.summary: Clause 15 affords profit and capital gain exemptions through end-2027, while a GST increase delay is fully precluded only for 2021, with the hike stated to occur by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Perhaps, most inexplicably, clause 15 affords profit and capital gain exemptions through till the end of 2027.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But I would note that a delay in increasing the burden of the major tax faced by workers, which is the Goods and Services Tax, is only fully precluded for 2021, with Minister Heng stating that the GST hike will occur by 2025.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill despite additional points of feedback.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding these additional points of feedback, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Repeal and re-enact section 33
sections.summary: The Bill proposes to repeal and re-enact section 33, which lets the Comptroller disregard tax avoidance arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes to repeal and re-enact section 33, which allows the Comptroller to disregard tax avoidance arrangements.

sections.label: Existing tax avoidance test
sections.summary: The question asks if the existing tax avoidance test in CIT vs AQQ still applies to the re-enacted section 33.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify if the existing test for tax avoidance in CIT vs AQQ continues to apply to the re-enacted section 33?

sections.label: New section 33(2) wording
sections.summary: The new section 33(2) proposed by the Bill replaces "may" with "must".

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 33(2) proposed by the Bill replaces "may" with "must".

sections.label: Remission of surcharge or interest
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to clarify when the surcharge or interest may be remitted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify under what circumstances the surcharge or interest may be remitted?

sections.label: Tax avoidance arrangement unchanged
sections.summary: What constitutes a tax avoidance arrangement does not change, and CIT vs AQQ principles continue to apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: What constitutes a tax avoidance arrangement does not change under the re-enacted section 33.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In other words, the principles set out in the CIT vs AQQ case will continue to apply and will assist the Comptroller of Income Tax in practice.

sections.label: Tax avoidance surcharge amendments
sections.summary: The Bill's surcharge and section 33 amendments reflect a strong stance against tax avoidance, with rare Comptroller remission of surcharge or interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Indeed, the proposed surcharge and other amendments to section 33, which we are proposing in this Bill, underscore our continued strong stance against tax avoidance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we do provide an avenue in the law for the Comptroller to remit the surcharge or interest on the surcharge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But I would stress that this remission would be rarely and judiciously exercised.
